title: TECHNICAL OPERATIONS / TICKETING AUTOMATION SPECIALIST
description:
Long-Term Role | Automation, Proxies, Technical Systems & Ticketing



PLEASE READ BEFORE APPLYING



We are currently completing recruitment for a separate Personal Assistant / Operations role, so although applications for this position are open now, interviews are unlikely to begin until around mid-October.



If you apply, please don’t worry if you don’t receive an immediate response. I am intentionally opening this position early so I can start finding the right person.



About the Role



I run a ticketing/resale business and am looking for a technically skilled person who can eventually take ownership of the technical and automation side of the business.



This is not necessarily a role for a senior software developer.



I am much more interested in someone who genuinely understands:



automation software

proxies and networking

browser automation

running multiple tasks efficiently

technical troubleshooting

APIs / webhooks / automation concepts

logs and error diagnosis

scaling software setups

testing different configurations

learning private or unfamiliar software quickly



I am willing to invest in the best software, tools, proxy providers, servers and infrastructure where it makes commercial sense.



What I need is somebody who understands the technical world well enough to make sure those tools are being used properly and efficiently.



What You Would Be Doing



During important ticket releases and on-sale events, you would be responsible for preparing our technical setup in advance and then operating the relevant automation software during the event.



This could include:



Configuring ticketing automation software before events

Preparing task files, accounts, payment information and event settings

Running multiple automated tasks during releases

Monitoring software while events are live

Diagnosing failed tasks or technical problems

Reviewing logs and identifying why something failed

Testing different setups to improve performance

Managing and testing proxy infrastructure

Comparing different proxy providers/types

Understanding which network setups perform best on different platforms

Researching new tools and technical methods

Speaking with software providers, developers and other experienced operators

Joining relevant private communities and learning from people already operating at a high level

Documenting successful configurations and processes

Advising me when better hardware, servers, VPSs or infrastructure would improve results



You would not be expected to build all of our software from scratch.



I am happy to purchase existing specialist software where appropriate.



The important part is that you understand the technology well enough to configure it, operate it, troubleshoot it, test it and continually improve the setup.



Proxies / Networking



This is a very important part of the position.



I am especially interested in candidates who understand areas such as:



Residential proxies

ISP proxies

Datacenter proxies

Mobile proxies

Static vs rotating proxies

Proxy authentication

Geo-location

Latency

Connection quality

Session persistence

Success rates

Proxy testing

Different providers and proxy pools

Diagnosing whether failures are caused by software, network, proxy quality or another part of the setup



You do not need to know absolutely everything on day one, but you should already be technically comfortable with this world.



If the word proxy means little more to you than changing your IP address, this probably isn’t the right role.



Coding / Development



Coding experience is a bonus, not a strict requirement.



It would be useful if you have experience with things such as:



Python

JavaScript

Browser automation

APIs

Webhooks

JSON

Playwright / Selenium

Google Apps Script

n8n

Make

Zapier

GitHub

VS Code / Cursor

Claude / Claude Code

AI-assisted development



For example, if a repetitive workflow could be improved with a simple browser script or automation, it would be great if you could build or adapt something yourself.



However, I am not hiring you primarily to build complex software from scratch.



Technical understanding, troubleshooting and operating systems effectively are more important.



Hardware / Infrastructure



Initially, you may operate tools from your own computer.



A reliable device and strong internet connection are therefore important.



However, I am completely open to investing in better infrastructure if needed.



For example:



VPS

cloud servers

remote desktops

dedicated machines

upgraded hardware

improved internet/networking

additional proxy services



I do not expect you to personally fund these things.



If you believe we need better infrastructure to scale, I want you to be capable of researching the options, explaining them to me in simple terms and helping set them up.



Research & Networking



A lot of the best information in this industry is not publicly documented.



I can provide access to people and communities where experienced operators discuss software, infrastructure and new developments.



I already have strong relationships within the ticketing world.



What I need is somebody technical enough to understand those conversations, ask the right questions and turn the information into something we can actually implement.



You should be naturally curious and enjoy:



investigating things

testing different setups

reading technical discussions

comparing tools

asking intelligent questions

figuring out how systems work

experimenting until something performs better

What I’m Looking For



The ideal person is:



Very comfortable with computers

Technically curious

Independent

Hard-working

Ambitious

Analytical

Patient when troubleshooting

Comfortable researching things they do not understand

Able to explain technical issues in simple English

Interested in automation

Interested in networking/proxies

Comfortable learning private/unfamiliar software

Someone who actually enjoys the “geeky” side of technology



This is not a role where you can message me every time something technical goes wrong.



I am not a developer myself.



I can provide the business context, money for tools, access to the right people and a clear commercial goal.



You need to be the person who can figure out the technical side.



Long-Term Opportunity



This is intended to become a long-term position.



Initially, the work may be more event-based while we build the setup and determine exactly how much ongoing work is required.



Longer term, I expect this person to become the main technical person within the ticketing business.



We already have other VAs handling administrative ticketing tasks.



Your role would sit above much of that operational work from a technical perspective.



As the business grows, you may eventually:



own the technical infrastructure

choose and test new tools

improve automation processes

coordinate technical projects

advise on software/infrastructure purchases

potentially help recruit or manage additional technical staff if required



I am looking for somebody who could potentially work with the business for years, not a short-term freelancer.



Working Hours



This is still being finalised.



The role could initially be:



event/project based



or potentially become:



a regular Monday–Friday position



The key requirement is that you must be available for important ticket releases and events, because that is when the systems need to be operated and monitored.



Some releases may take place outside normal Philippine working hours.



Flexibility will therefore be important.



Salary / Compensation



To be discussed.



I understand this is a more technical position than a standard VA role.



At the same time, the business is still building toward the point where this technical operation can scale significantly, so I am not currently looking to hire an expensive senior developer.



I am particularly interested in a junior or mid-level technical person with strong potential, who wants to grow alongside the business.



Depending on the candidate and structure of the role, compensation could potentially involve:



fixed monthly salary

project/event-based payments

performance/profit-based bonuses

or a combination



We can discuss this properly with the right candidates.



How to Apply



Start your application with the word:



PROXY



Then answer the following questions:



Tell me about your technical background.

What operating systems do you regularly use?

Explain your experience with proxies.

What is the difference between residential, ISP, datacenter and mobile proxies?

Have you ever tested different proxy providers or proxy pools? How did you compare them?

Have you ever worked with browser automation or automation software?

Have you used Python, JavaScript, Playwright, Selenium, Puppeteer or similar tools?

Have you worked with APIs, webhooks or JSON?

Have you ever used a VPS, cloud server, remote desktop or dedicated server?

Have you used tools such as n8n, Make or Zapier?

Do you use ChatGPT, Claude, Claude Code, Cursor or other AI coding tools?

Tell me about a technical problem you had to solve where you initially did not know the answer.

If I gave you unfamiliar software with limited documentation and asked you to learn it, configure it and operate it independently, how would you approach it?

How would you determine whether a failed task was caused by:

the software

the proxy/network

the account/session

the website

or the computer/server itself?

What computer do you currently use? Please include:

CPU

RAM

operating system

internet speed if known

What are your normal working hours in Philippine time?

Would you be available outside normal hours for important ticket releases?

What monthly salary or compensation structure would you be looking for?

Are you looking for something temporary, or would you be interested in becoming the long-term technical person for one business?

Why does this particular position interest you?



Please do not worry if you do not hear from me immediately. Interviews are expected to begin around mid-October while I finish hiring for another position first.

title: Solar Project Coordinator
description:
Mālama Solar is looking for an experienced Solar Project Coordinator based in the Philippines to help manage residential solar projects through permitting, utility approval, and other pre-installation milestones.



Hawaiʻi solar experience is required for this position. We are specifically looking for someone who has previously worked on residential solar projects in Hawaiʻi and understands the permitting and utility approval process.



This is not an entry-level solar position. We are looking for someone who can step in, understand the workflow, stay organized, follow up consistently, and help move projects forward without needing constant supervision.



What You’ll Be Responsible For



You will help manage solar projects from completed sale through installation readiness, including:



Preparing and submitting permit applications

Tracking building permit approvals with Hawaiʻi permitting jurisdictions

Preparing and submitting utility/interconnection applications

Working with HECO and related utility approval processes

Monitoring projects for missing documents, corrections, and outstanding requirements

Responding to permit and utility correction requests

Following up regularly on applications that are waiting for approval

Coordinating with design, engineering, sales, operations, and installation teams

Keeping project statuses, notes, documents, and deadlines updated in our systems

Identifying projects that are stalled and taking action to move them forward

Communicating clearly with internal team members regarding project status and next steps

Helping ensure projects are fully ready before they are released for installation



Depending on experience, you may also assist with HOA approvals, NEM/interconnection documentation, inspection-related paperwork, equipment changes, and other project coordination tasks.



Required Experience



Please do not apply unless you have previous solar experience in Hawaiʻi.



Qualified applicants should have experience with several of the following:



Residential solar permitting in Hawaiʻi

HECO interconnection or utility applications

City & County of Honolulu permitting

Hawaiʻi County, Maui County, or Kauaʻi permitting

Solar plansets and permit documentation

Battery storage projects

PV + battery projects

Permit corrections and resubmissions

Utility corrections and resubmissions

Project management or solar operations

CRM/project management software



Experience working with products such as Tesla Powerwall, Enphase, FranklinWH, or similar solar and battery systems is helpful.



What We’re Looking For



The right person is:



Extremely organized

Excellent at follow-up

Detail-oriented

Comfortable managing a large number of projects at once

Proactive rather than waiting to be told what to do

Good at finding missing information and solving problems

Able to communicate clearly in written English

Comfortable working with a U.S.-based team

Reliable and consistent

Able to prioritize projects based on urgency and next steps



A major part of this position is simply making sure that nothing falls through the cracks.



We want someone who looks at their project list every day and asks:



“What can I do today to move each of these projects forward?”



Work Schedule



This is a full-time remote position based in the Philippines.



Because you will be working with our Hawaiʻi team, applicants must be comfortable having some overlap with Hawaiʻi business hours.



About Mālama Solar



Mālama Solar is a Hawaiʻi-based residential solar and battery company serving homeowners throughout the islands. We have completed thousands of solar projects and work with many of the leading solar, battery, utility, and financing providers in the industry.

title: Logo Vectorisation Supervisor

.

* Experience in cosmetics, beauty, CPG, or manufacturing is a plus.

* A degree in Industrial Engineering, Supply Chain Management, Logistics, Packaging Engineering, or a related field is preferred but not required.

title: Long-Term Video Editor – E-Commerce, Meta Ads & AI
description:
We’re looking for a seriously talented Video Editor to join our team long-term.



But we want to make one thing clear from the beginning:



We’re not just looking for someone who can edit videos.



We’re a group of guys aged 19, 20, and 21 building and scaling e-commerce brands together. We’re extremely ambitious, move fast, test a lot of creatives, and genuinely enjoy what we do.



We want to find an editor who has that same hunger.



Someone who genuinely loves editing, understands what makes content perform, follows what’s happening in the ad/content world, and constantly wants to become better.



We also don’t want the relationship to feel like:



“Here’s a task → edit it → send it back.”



We want you to become part of the team.



Someone we can brainstorm with, joke around with, share ideas with, learn together with, and hopefully build a genuine friendship with over time.



If we win, we want you to win with us.



What We’re Looking For



You should:



Be very good in Adobe Premiere Pro

Have an understanding of After Effects

Do NOT apply if CapCut is your main editing software

Have experience creating AI Avatars / AI-generated content

Have a strong understanding of Meta Ads and performance creatives

Understand hooks, retention, pacing, storytelling and direct-response editing

Stay updated with what’s currently working in the feed

Understand that a good editor doesn't just make something look pretty — the goal is to make people stop, watch and buy

Be comfortable testing different editing styles and creative concepts

Be able to take feedback without ego and improve quickly

Be proactive and bring your own ideas instead of always waiting for instructions

Care about the small details

Be reliable and communicate well

Most importantly: actually love what you do

The Type of Person We Want



We care a lot about skill.



But we care just as much about who you are as a person.



We’d rather work with someone hungry, positive and obsessed with improving than someone technically amazing who doesn’t care about the work.



We’re young, ambitious and have very big goals.



We want someone who thinks:



“I want to become one of the best editors at what I do.”



Not:



“How quickly can I finish this task?”



There is a big difference.



For the right person, we want this to become a long-term position where you grow alongside us as the brands and team grow.



How To Apply



Please send us:



1. Your portfolio — especially Meta ads, e-commerce creatives, UGC/direct-response ads and AI avatar work.



2. Tell us about yourself — not just your work experience. We want to know who we might be working with every day.



3. Tell us what editing software you use and what you're strongest at.



4. Tell us about your experience editing Meta Ads.



5. Show us any AI Avatar / AI content you've created.



And if you really want to stand out, send us a short voice note or video introduction explaining who you are, why you think you'd fit our team, and why we should choose you.



🔐 Secret word



If you actually read this entire job post, start your application with:



“PINEAPPLE” 🍍



Applications without the secret word will not be prioritized.



We’re excited to meet you.



We’re not looking for someone to edit a few videos. We’re looking for the next person to become part of our team and build something big with us.

title: Paid Media Buyer (Performance Marketing)
description:
USD $1,000–$1,400 / month | Full-Time | Remote | Hire by Sep 30th! | Philippine hours



---



Are you a performance marketer who wants to learn how a top e-com / DTC team actually scales paid — inside a brand that went from zero to ~$100M USD in under three years?



Apply below for a role where you either grow newer ad channels or turn agency creatives into revenue — and build a track record with one of the strongest growth teams in the space.







---



[1] About Ally



Ally helps founders and leaders scale themselves before they scale their companies.



We match Executive Partners with fast-growing e-commerce and creative businesses, combining human judgment with modern AI systems.



We're not a traditional VA agency. We're a modern operating partner.



This seat sits with one of our clients — a DTC brand that scaled from zero to ~$100M USD in under three years. You work inside their marketing team, with Ally behind you.



---



[2] The Role



You'll own paid performance in one of two shapes (same rate, same bar):



- Channel Owner — take newer paid channels (TikTok, Snapchat, Reddit, Taboola) and grow them so they carry real revenue on their own. There is no finished playbook; you write it as you learn.

- Agency Ads — get agency creatives live within two days, test properly, and scale winners. Measured on what they earn, not how much got uploaded.



You buy/run the ads, watch the numbers every day, and tell the team what they mean. Leadership does not open the platforms — they read your report. First one to two months, recommendations go to the marketing lead; then you optimise alone inside a ROAS floor.



---



[3] What You'll Do



- Keep your channels or agency ads running and growing (spend, accounts, billing flags, replacements when something gets rejected)

- Build the daily report — right every day, with what happened, why, and what to do next

- Launch at volume (often 100–200 ads/day) with clean structure

- D
 what to scale, cut, and test — with approval at first, then yours

- For Agency Ads: watch for new assets, get them live fast, tell agencies what to make more of

- Spot problems and opportunities before anyone asks

- Draft advertorials with AI; bring one outside idea to test each week



You will not design creatives. Internal team + agencies produce assets; you shape what they make from the data.



---



[4] What We're Looking For



- You've bought media with real spend and can read the numbers — not just upload

- You catch a wrong number before the reader does

- Initiative — see it, do it

- You ask constantly; a quiet week is a warning sign

- Creative judgment — which ad is the real winner, and what angle to make more of

- Clear reporting for a non-technical reader

- Open to newer channels (TikTok / Snapchat / Reddit / Taboola). Hands-on time there is rare and we notice it

- Bulk tooling (AdManage / Revealbot) or able to pick it up in two weeks



---



[5] What You'll Get



- USD $1,000–$1,400 / month to start, full-time, remote, Philippine hours

- Two weeks one-to-one with the marketing lead, then real decision rights once earned

- Real spend on a brand that scaled $0 → ~$100M — a track record with numbers attached

- The playbook for your channels with your name on it (Channel Owner)

- Paid tools; direct access to the operators you work with



---



[6] Schedule



5 days a week, 8am–5pm Philippine time. One of your five days is on a weekend so the team always has coverage. Days confirmed when we assign you.



---



[7] How to Apply



Submit here:







1. Upload your CV and provide your LinkedIn profile URL (both required)

2. Record one short Loom (2–3 mins total):

   - Briefly introduce yourself and your relevant paid media experience

   - Which platforms you've actually run paid on (especially TikTok, Snapchat, Reddit, Taboola), and which you haven't

   - Answer: Last 7 days — Ad A $120 / 1 purchase / $95; Ad B $2,400 / 41 / $4,300; Ad C $310 / 6 / $680. Which would you scale, and why? (~1 min)



No video, no shortlist. Applications outside this link are not reviewed.

title: Content Researcher & Social Media Analyst
description:
Content Researcher & Social Media Analyst



Type of Employment: Full-Time

Salary: $800–$1,200 USD/month depending on experience



About the Role



We are looking for an experienced Content Researcher & Social Media Analyst to join our content team full-time.



This is not a basic VA or data-entry research position.



We are looking for someone who genuinely understands social media content, has experience working with content that has generated results, and knows how to identify why certain content performs and why other content doesn't.



You will be responsible for researching content and generating ideas for the personal brands and businesses we work with.



A major part of your job will be studying what is currently working across platforms such as Instagram, TikTok, YouTube,
 and X, identifying patterns, and turning those findings into actionable content ideas for our team.



What You'll Be Doing



You will:



- Research high-performing content across Instagram, TikTok, YouTube,
, X and other relevant platforms.

- Study competitors, creators and pages within each client's industry.

- Identify high-performing topics, hooks, formats, angles and content structures.

- Analyze why certain pieces of content performed well.

- Analyze underperforming content and identify what could have been improved.

- Track emerging trends and changes in what is working across social media.

- Research topics and ideas relevant to each client's target audience.

- Turn your research into specific content ideas our creative team can actually execute.

- Analyze our clients' existing content and use performance data to help determine what we should create more or less of.

- Find successful content from other industries that could be adapted to our clients.

- Build organized research documents, competitor databases and idea banks for each client.

- Work closely with our content team to continuously improve our creative strategy.



We don't just want someone who can say, "This video got 2 million views."



We want someone who can break it down and explain:



Why did it get 2 million views?



Was it the topic? The hook? The framing? The format? The person? The timing? The storytelling? The controversy? The value provided?



And most importantly:



How can we use that insight to create something great for our clients?



What We're Looking For



You should have:



- Previous experience working with social media content.

- Evidence that content you researched, strategized or worked on has generated strong results.

- A strong understanding of modern short-form and long-form content.

- A very good understanding of Instagram Reels, TikTok, YouTube Shorts and YouTube.

- Experience researching competitors, creators, trends and viral content.

- Strong analytical skills — you naturally want to understand why something worked.

- Experience using modern social media research, analytics, trend-discovery and AI tools.

- The ability to find information quickly and efficiently.

- Strong written English and communication skills.

- Excellent attention to detail and organization.

 The ability to work independently and bring us ideas rather than waiting to be told exactly what to research.



Very Important



We are specifically looking for someone with real content experience.



When applying, please send:



- A short explanation of your previous experience with social media/content.

- Examples of content you have worked on and the results it generated.

- The social media research and analytics tools you currently use.

- Three examples of creators or brands you think are doing an exceptional job with content right now and briefly explain why.

- Pick one piece of content that has performed extremely well recently and give us a short breakdown of why you believe it performed.



- Please include the word “ANALYST” at the beginning of your application so we know you have read the full job description.



We are looking for someone who wants to become an important part of our content team long-term and help us consistently produce better content for our clients.

title: Amazon Inventory FBA Analyst (Full-time / Long term)
description:
Supply Chain & Inventory Analyst – Amazon FBA 



We're building out our Amazon USA private label operations team, and we're looking for a sharp, detail-oriented Amazon FBA Inventory Analyst to grow into a future Operations Manager. 



This is an entry-to-mid-level role for someone who already has hands-on Amazon FBA / supply chain analyst experience and wants a clear path toward owning end-to-end operations.



You'll work closely with our Supply Chain Manager and leadership team, learning every part of the business — from supplier production in China, to 3PL warehousing, to Amazon FBA — while taking ownership of forecasting, inventory health, and account operations.



## Highlights



- Full-time, 40 hours/week

- Competitive salary based on experience

- Performance-based incentives/bonuses

- Clear growth path into an Operations Manager role

- Remote position

- Health insurance stipend

- Paid vacation



## Key Responsibilities



**Inventory & Supply Chain**

- Track inventory levels across 3PL and Amazon FBA; flag stockout or overstock risks early.

- Support and eventually help manage monthly and seasonal demand forecasts.

- Monitor inbound shipments, POs, and lead times from suppliers through to FBA receiving.

- Help troubleshoot logistics issues — customs delays, inbound shipment problems, 3PL discrepancies.



**Amazon Marketplace Support**

- Monitor Amazon account health metrics and flag policy or listing issues to the team.

- Support order management and coordinate with customer service on account-related issues.

- Keep an eye on product listings, rankings, and competitor activity.

- Coordinate with the PPC team so ad spend aligns with current inventory levels.



**Vendor & Purchasing Support**

- Assist with supplier and freight forwarder communication and follow-ups.

- Track vendor performance (on-time delivery, quality) and flag issues.

- Support purchasing activities and cost-tracking.



**Growth & Development**

- Work directly alongside the Operations Manager/Supply Chain Manager to learn strategic decision-making.

- Take on increasing ownership of forecasting, vendor relationships, and account health over time.

- As you build track record against the KPIs above, grow into managing your own reports and eventually the Operations Manager role.



## Qualifications (Must-Have)



- 3 years of experience as an Amazon Supply Chain Specialist, Amazon Inventory/FBA Analyst, or similar supply chain analyst role.

- Working knowledge of Amazon FBA logistics and inventory management.

- Comfortable with data — pulling reports, spotting trends, building basic forecasts.

- Highly organized, detail-oriented, and process-driven.

- Comfortable in a fast-paced, high-growth environment with partial overlap to U.S. East Coast time zone.

- Fluent in English; strong written and analytical communication.

- Eager to grow into a leadership/management role over time.



## Nice to Have



- Exposure to international shipping/logistics (China to USA), customs, or freight forwarding.

- Familiarity with forecasting tools or Amazon software (e.g., Helium 10, SoStocked).

- Familiarity with project management tools (ClickUp, Asana).

- Proficiency in Google Sheets/Excel for analysis and reporting.

- Ability to speak Mandarin (a plus, not required).

1. Walk us through the role where you had the most hands-on Amazon FBA and Seller Central experience: what was your day-to-day, and roughly how many SKUs or how much inventory value were you responsible for?



2. Tell us about a time you had to forecast demand or manage inventory levels to avoid a stockout or overstock situation. What data or method did you use, and what was the outcome?



3. Describe the trickiest Amazon account or operational issue you've resolved — could be a policy violation, IP complaint, inbound shipment problem, or 3PL/supplier issue. What did you do and how did it turn out?

6. Our company uses time tracker to pay contractors, are you comfortable with this?

Thank you and God bless!

title: Video Editor & Content Producer
description:
Video Editor & Content Producer



25–35 Hours/Week | Long-Term | Sport, Events & E-Commerce



We’re an Australian company looking for a talented Video Editor & Content Producer to become a long-term part of our creative team.



We’re looking for approximately 30 hours per week, with flexibility around working hours. For the right person, there is potential for the role to grow.



This is not a role where you simply wait for someone to tell you where to make every cut.



We want someone who can take raw footage, understand what we’re trying to achieve, identify the strongest stories and hooks, and turn it into engaging content quickly.



You’ll work across two very different businesses, which means the content is varied and there is always something new to create.



WORLD OCEAN SERIES — SPORT & EVENTS



We run a growing Australian ocean sports and events series.



Our team captures a huge amount of content around our events: elite racing, athlete stories, interviews, behind-the-scenes footage, B-roll, crowds, entertainment, sponsors, activations and everything happening around the event.



We want to dramatically improve the speed at which that raw footage becomes great content.



You might create:



* Fast-paced race highlights

* Athlete stories and profiles

* Behind-the-scenes content

* Reels, TikToks and Shorts

* Event hype videos

* Sponsor content and activations

* Event recaps and highlight packages

* Longer-form storytelling

* Content promoting the entire event experience — live sport, music, food, entertainment and atmosphere

* Multiple versions of content for different audiences and platforms



You don’t need to already understand ocean sports.



But you do need to understand sport, competition and storytelling — and be a quick learner.



Over time, we want you to know our athletes, events and storylines well enough that you can look through footage and identify what matters without us having to explain everything.



You’ll also work directly with the people shooting our content.



We want you to be able to say:



“We need more of this.”



“Next event, let’s capture this angle.”



“There’s a story here.”



“Give me more athlete reactions and less generic B-roll.”



You won’t just sit at the end of the production process. You’ll help us make the whole process better.



E-COMMERCE & AD CREATIVE



We also operate a fast-growing e-commerce business.



Here, the objective is different.



We need a constant pipeline of fresh, engaging advertising creative.



You’ll work with product footage, UGC, photography, existing ads and new content to create and test different ideas.



This could include:



* New hooks and opening sequences

* Multiple variations of successful ads

* UGC edits

* Product-focused ads

* Graphic overlays

* Motion graphics and simple animation

* Different music, pacing and messaging

* Fresh angles using existing footage

* Testing different lengths and formats

* Rapidly iterating on creative that is performing well



You should understand that an ad isn’t just a nice-looking video. It has a job to do.



Sometimes that’s stopping the scroll.



Sometimes it’s generating a click.



Sometimes it’s explaining a product.



Sometimes it’s creating desire.



Sometimes it’s taking something that’s already working and producing five intelligent variations to see if we can make it work even better.



We want someone interested in understanding why content performs, not just whether it looks good.



WHAT WE’RE LOOKING FOR



Technical editing ability matters, but we’re looking for more than someone who knows editing software.



We want someone who:



* Has excellent instincts for short-form content

* Understands hooks, pacing, retention and storytelling

* Understands sport and competition

* Can identify interesting moments in raw footage

* Can work without needing every edit mapped out

* Can create multiple variations quickly

* Understands the difference between organic content and performance advertising

* Can use graphics, text, overlays and animation where they improve the content

* Is comfortable receiving feedback and iterating quickly

* Can learn our brands, athletes and audiences

* Is organised with large volumes of footage

* Can work directly with the people filming our content

* Is interested in improving the entire production workflow, not just editing individual videos

* Is curious about what performs and why



We care about speed AND quality.



We don’t want someone spending an entire day perfecting a 20-second Reel that could have been excellent in two hours.



We also don’t want someone pumping out mediocre content just to hit a volume target.



Our goal is to build a production system where great footage becomes great content fast.



HOURS & WORKING WITH US



This is an ongoing, long-term role averaging approximately 25–35 hours per week.



There is flexibility around your working hours.



We’re much more interested in finding an excellent person than forcing a traditional 40-hour work week.



However, we’re not looking for someone who occasionally picks up editing jobs when they have spare time.



We want someone who can become a consistent part of our team, learn our businesses deeply and take increasing ownership of our content production.



If the relationship works well, there is plenty of opportunity for the role to grow.



WHAT SUCCESS LOOKS LIKE



Initially, we’ll provide more direction while you learn our businesses.



But over time, we want to be able to send you a folder containing footage from an event and have you start saying:



“This is a story.”



“This could make a great Reel.”



“There are three different pieces of content in this footage.”



“We should create several versions of this.”



“Next time, the camera team should capture this angle.”



Likewise, with our e-commerce creative, we want you looking at what’s performing and thinking:



“Why is this working?”



“What happens if we change the first three seconds?”



“Can we create five new versions without needing another shoot?”



That’s the level we’re trying to build toward.



HOW TO APPLY



Please do not send us a generic application.



Start your application with the words:

title: Generative AI Visual Artist (Image & Video)
description:
IMPORTANT: To be considered for this role, you must submit your CV/resume, a short intro video, and samples of your previous work or portfolio. Applications without these three requirements will not be reviewed.



We are looking for a highly creative and technically capable Generative AI Visual Artist who can create photorealistic AI characters, environments, imagery, and video content at a professional production level.



This is not a traditional graphic design position. We are specifically looking for someone who already works hands-on with generative AI tools for image and video creation and understands how to turn a creative brief into polished, realistic, production-ready visual assets.



Your main responsibility will be helping create the visual identity, expressions, environments, and overall presence of AI-powered digital characters. The goal is to make these characters feel believable, consistent, polished, and visually engaging across different images, scenes, poses, and video sequences.



You will create high-quality, photorealistic character assets, facial expressions, poses, backgrounds, and environments. You will use generative AI image and video tools to explore creative concepts, iterate quickly, and produce final visuals that meet a clear creative direction.



A major part of this role is maintaining character consistency. You should understand how to keep the same character recognizable across different camera angles, expressions, poses, clothing, environments, and sequences. You should be comfortable using conditioning, reference images, control techniques, and other methods that help maintain composition, character identity, and visual style.



You will also work extensively with generative video. You should have practical experience with image-to-video, video-to-video, AI motion generation, and similar workflows. We are looking for someone who understands how to create believable movement while maintaining visual quality and character consistency across a sequence.



You should also be capable of taking AI-generated output beyond the initial generation. This may include improving lighting, perspective, composition, realism, continuity, and overall quality. You should be comfortable identifying AI artifacts and inconsistencies and correcting them through multimodal editing, compositing, retouching, digital painting, or other finishing techniques.



The ideal candidate has strong professional experience creating visual content in areas such as film, VFX, animation, gaming, digital art, advertising, or another high-quality visual production environment. Direct experience working professionally with generative AI imagery and video is strongly preferred.



You should have an excellent visual eye and a strong understanding of composition, lighting, color, perspective, camera angles, lenses, depth, and continuity. We need someone who can look critically at their own work, quickly identify what does not look right, and continue refining it until the final result reaches a high quality standard.



Experience with node-based AI workflows or production pipelines is highly valuable. You should be comfortable experimenting with different tools, building repeatable workflows, testing new AI platforms, and finding better ways to consistently produce high-quality visual assets.



Experience with tools related to AI avatars, generative video, voice, or conversational AI is also a plus. Familiarity with platforms such as Tavus, Anam, LemonSlice, ElevenLabs, Cartesia, or similar technologies would be helpful, but we are also open to candidates who have strong experience with other advanced AI image and video tools.



We care much more about the quality of your work than a specific degree. A strong portfolio showing photorealistic AI imagery, consistent AI characters, AI-generated video, motion work, VFX, animation, or similar visual production will be one of the most important parts of your application.



You should be creative, detail-oriented, highly comfortable experimenting with new technology, and able to work independently while also collaborating with product, design, and marketing teams. You should be willing to test ideas quickly, accept feedback, refine your work, and continuously improve your creative process.



This is a remote opportunity with flexibility depending on the right candidate and may be structured as part-time or full-time.



HOW TO APPLY



Please send your CV/resume, a short intro video introducing yourself and explaining your experience with generative AI, and a portfolio or links to your best sample work.



In your intro video, briefly explain which AI image and video tools you currently use, how long you have been working with generative AI, and what type of AI visual work you are strongest at.



For your portfolio, we especially want to see examples of photorealistic AI characters, character consistency across multiple images, AI-generated video, image-to-video work, realistic environments, animation, VFX, or other advanced generative visual work.



We are looking for someone who combines a strong artistic eye with real hands-on AI production skills and can consistently turn AI-generated content into professional-quality visual experiences.

title: Full-Time Funding Client Coordinator / Closer
description:
I am looking for a reliable, organized, and confident **Client Funding Coordinator / Closer** to help manage clients for a U.S.-based business funding company.



This is a **full-time, long-term position (40 hours per week).**



**Leads are provided. You are NOT responsible for finding or generating your own leads.** Your primary responsibility is to work with the leads provided, communicate with clients, follow up consistently, help them through the funding process, and help convert qualified opportunities into successfully closed deals.



I am specifically looking for someone who already has **some experience in business funding, lending, MCA, business loans, loan processing, or a closely related financial-services environment.**



You should already understand basic funding terminology and be comfortable speaking with clients, following up persistently, handling objections, and helping move deals toward closing.



### Responsibilities



* Work with leads provided to you

* Contact new leads by phone, text, and

* Speak with U.S.-based business owners

* Follow up consistently with leads and active applicants

* Help clients complete funding applications

* Follow up on incomplete applications

* Request and track required documents and information

* Monitor applications throughout the funding process

* Respond to requests for additional information

* Keep clients engaged throughout the process

* Explain funding-process next steps clearly

* Handle basic client questions using provided information and training

* Follow up on funding offers, outstanding requirements, and signatures

* Handle objections professionally and help move qualified clients toward closing

* Track each client from initial contact through funding

* Maintain accurate CRM notes, tasks, and pipeline stages

* Follow up with older leads when appropriate

* Provide a short daily pipeline and closing report

* Escalate situations requiring my attention



You will receive training on my specific systems, CRM, processes, and scripts.



You will **not make underwriting or funding decisions**. However, this is **not simply a data-entry or administrative VA position**. I need someone who is confident speaking with clients, understands the basics of funding, and is motivated to help move deals toward closing.



### Social Media Bonus Skill—NOT MANDATORY



When the client/funding workload is lighter, I would love someone who can also help with:



* Creating simple social media posts



This is not mandatory. Only if you want to. 



### Compensation



**Base salary: $600/month**



PLUS a performance bonus for every successfully closed deal where the company receives its fee:



**1–4 closed deals/month:** $100 per closed deal

**5–8 closed deals/month:** $125 per closed deal

**9+ closed deals/month:** $150 per closed deal



The business currently targets approximately **4 successfully closed deals per month.**



For example:



**4 closed deals = $600 base + $400 bonus = $1000 total compensation for the month.**



There is significant opportunity to earn more as the number of successfully closed deals increases.



A bonus is earned after the deal successfully funds and the company receives its fee.



### REQUIRED Experience



Please apply only if you have at least some previous experience with one or more of the following:



* Business funding

* Business loans

* MCA / merchant cash advance

* Lending

* Loan processing

* Funding brokerage

* Financial-services sales

* Similar funding or lending environment



You should already be familiar with basic terminology such as **underwriting, funding amount, approval, offer, lender, bank statements, revenue, credit, documents/stipulations, funded, declined, and closing.**



### I Am Looking For Someone Who



* Has excellent spoken and written English

* Is confident speaking with U.S.-based clients

* Is comfortable making outbound and follow-up calls

* Has strong sales and closing skills

* Can handle objections professionally

* Is persistent and consistent with follow-ups

* Understands basic funding/lending terminology

* Is comfortable working in a CRM

* Is organized and detail-oriented

* Can manage multiple active clients simultaneously

* Can work independently

* Is professional with confidential client information

* Is motivated by performance-based compensation

* **Bonus:** Comfortable with Canva, AI tools, and social media content creation



### Schedule



**Full-time — 40 hours per week, Monday through Friday.**



Exact working hours will be discussed during the interview.



### How to Apply



Please answer ALL of the following:



1. What experience do you have in business funding, lending, MCA, business loans, or financial services?

2. What funding/lending terminology are you already familiar with?

3. Have you previously spoken with U.S.-based clients by phone?

4. Have you ever been responsible for closing deals or converting leads? Please explain.

5. How would you handle a client who is interested but keeps delaying their application or documents?

6. What CRM systems have you used?

7. Approximately how many calls or client follow-ups did you handle per day in your previous role?

8. Do you have experience with **Canva, AI tools, or managing social media?**

9. Please provide examples of social media work if available.

10. What hours are you available to work?



**You do not need to generate leads. Leads will be provided.**



Please do **not** apply if you have only general administrative/data-entry experience and no funding, lending, financial-services, or relevant sales experience.

title: Short-Form Video Editor for Daily Instagram Reels (CapCut, Long-Term, Start This Week)
description:
I sell a product to local business owners. I walk into their store, talk to the owner, and try to sell to them. I record everything on Meta glasses on my face. I post 5 Reels a day on Instagram. The account is 16 days old and has done over 2.4 million views. I need one editor long-term to handle the edits and the scheduling.



Read this whole post before you apply. It is long on purpose and there are 5 steps at the bottom. I ignore every application that skips a step.



Here is how the work runs. This is not a daily deadline job. Every week I film 7 days of footage and dump all of it into a shared Google Drive folder. Sunday night I close that week's folder and message you. You then have the entire following week to turn that footage into 40 finished clips. 35 of them are for my Instagram. The other 5 are for a separate client project with a different format that I will brief you on separately, and those are delivered as files rather than scheduled.



There are two points in your week. By Wednesday I want 20 clips sitting in the folder. That is a progress check, not a delivery date, because nothing actually goes live until the following Monday. It exists so that if a week is going badly we both find out on Wednesday instead of Sunday night. Then by Sunday night, all 40 are finished and sitting in the folder, ready for the week starting Monday. Once you are doing the publishing too, that means uploaded, captioned and scheduled by Sunday night as well. Between those two points you work whenever you want. Do 10 clips one day and none the next. If you finish everything by Thursday and take the rest of the week off, that is a perfect week and I will not message you.



I want to be straight with you about the workload because I would rather lose you now than in week two. 40 clips a week at 20 to 45 minutes a clip is 13 to 30 hours of editing, plus going through the raw footage on top of that. Call it 3 to 4 hours a day. I film 30 to 40 businesses a day, so a week's folder is usually around 300 visits and you only need 40 clips out of it, but you are still going through most of that footage to find them. I am telling you that so it is not a surprise later. What you get in exchange is that you are never forced to squeeze clips out of a dead day. If Tuesday was garbage, skip Tuesday and pull more from Thursday.



Run that math yourself before you answer. If it does not work for you, please do not apply, and there are no hard feelings. I also need you to commit to at least 4 weeks. I have had an editor take this job and leave after 3 days, and that cost me a week of my schedule.



The pay is $300 a month, paid $70 every week through Wise or PayPal after that week is delivered. The rate is tied to the volume, so if the weekly clip count ever changes, the pay changes with it.



Now the raw files. My glasses have a 5 minute recording limit, so they stop automatically. I also turn them off myself sometimes, like when an owner tells me to come back in 10 minutes. That means one visit to one business often comes to you as 2, 3, or more separate files. The files come in unsorted with names like IMG plus random numbers. Sorting them and working out which files belong to which visit is part of the job.



Every finished video is one visit to one business, beginning to end. One video equals one story about one customer. If a visit was recorded across 4 files, all 4 go together in order and become one video. Never mix footage from different businesses into the same video. When you join files from the same visit, cut the dead time off the end of one and the start of the next so the viewer cannot tell the recording stopped. Skip footage where the person is not conversational or their English is hard to follow. I dump everything I record and not all of it is usable.



I post 5 Reels a day at 9 AM, 12 PM, 2 PM, 5 PM and 8 PM. 3 of them are rejections, where the owner says no, and 2 are sales, where the owner buys. The sales go at 12 PM and 8 PM. The rejections go at 9 AM, 2 PM and 5 PM. So out of your 35 Instagram clips a week, 21 are rejections and 14 are sales. Do not force a boring clip in just to hit the number. A boring video is worse than no video. If a week genuinely cannot produce the mix, tell me and tell me what it can produce.



Now how I want them edited. Fast, no dead air. Cut long pauses, my stutters and ums, long walking, and silence while the owner is thinking. If nothing is happening on screen, remove it.



Read this next part carefully, because most editors go too far one way. Fast editing does not mean cutting every 2 seconds. Do not manufacture cuts to make it feel busy. The rule is simple. If nothing is happening, cut it. If something is happening, leave it alone. If I am walking across a parking lot for 40 seconds, cut it to 3 seconds. But if the owner is talking, asking questions, reacting, or going back and forth with me, that is the interesting part and it stays exactly as it is. Some clips will have very few cuts in the middle because the conversation is good the whole way through. That is correct editing, not lazy editing. And never remove the story. The viewer has to understand what happened from beginning to end.



Here is what you always cut out of a video. First, go watch my Instagram. You will see what I sell and how I sell it. Before I walk into a business I set the product up on my phone. I almost always do this in my car, so it is usually not recorded at all. But sometimes it ends up on camera. If you see it, cut it out. I never want a viewer to watch me setting the product up. I never want a viewer to learn how to do it. That is the only part of my process I keep private. You can show my phone. That is fine. You can show the app on my screen. That is also fine. The only thing you cut is the part where you can see me using the app to set the product up. Keep the moment the product works. Keep the customer's reaction to it. That is usually the best part of the whole video. Never cut that. Cut my personal information every single time. If I say my phone number out loud, cut it. If I write my phone number down, cut it. If my phone number is visible on screen, cut it. Same for my
. Same for anything else someone could use to contact me. Cut boring small talk. Talking about the weather is the usual example. But if the small talk is funny, keep it. Ask yourself one question. Is this interesting to watch? If yes, keep it. If no, cut it.



Every clip follows the same structure. A 3 to 5 second POV style hook text overlay at the top. Then cut straight to me getting out of my car, closing the door and walking to the store, with jump cuts so it feels fast. Then the conversation with the owner, which is the main part. Then the ending, me walking out, turning around, or reacting. Do not delete the ending. Clips run 45 seconds to 2 minutes 15 seconds. The length depends on the conversation. Never force a clip short.



On the technical side, everything is edited in CapCut and you supply your own CapCut Pro. Audio boosted 20 dB. Use meme sound effects like a BRUH or a laugh occasionally when something is funny, but not in every video.



The captions and text look identical on every single video and this is not something you change or get creative with. Captions are CapCut auto captions, Proxima Nova Extra Bold with bold turned on, color hex 00B209, using a specific CapCut text template I will show you in a screenshot. The hook overlay is Montserrat Extra Bold with bold turned on, centered at the top of the screen, placed where Instagram's buttons will not cover it. If you cannot find either of those exact fonts in your CapCut, message me before you pick a substitute. I will send you the font files. Do not quietly swap in something close.



Here is how you export. Use MP4. Use 1080p. Use 30 frames per second. Keep the file under 200 MB. In CapCut, set the project to original ratio. Do not set it to 9:16. Do not crop the video. Do not zoom in. Do not scale the video up to fill the screen. My footage already comes in close to vertical, so leave it exactly the size it is. When it gets posted, Instagram will add black bars at the top and bottom. That is normal. That is what I want. Do not try to fix it.



For all the text I will give you ChatGPT prompts. One for the hook overlay, and separate ones for the Instagram caption, the TikTok caption, and the YouTube Shorts title and description. You watch the clip first, write the context yourself based on what actually happened rather than guessing from the filename, run the prompt, and pick the funniest option. Not the first one. On some clips I say a specific line out loud near the end asking people to comment. When I do, that exact line goes in the caption word for word. When I do not say it, it does not go in.



You will also be publishing, but not right away. Here is how that works. First you do the paid test. Then you do your first full week of 40 clips. I will watch all of them and tell you what needs to change. Until I am happy with your editing, all you do is edit and put the finished files in the folder, and I publish them myself. Once your editing is where I want it, you take over the publishing. When that happens, I will add you to my OpusClip account as a Team Member. You get your own login. You will never have my password. You upload the clips there, paste in the copy from my prompts, tick Instagram, TikTok and YouTube Shorts, and schedule the whole week.



Before you tell me a week is done, check all of it. Play every exported file start to finish and confirm it actually works. Do that every single week, starting from your very first one. Once you are doing the publishing, there is more to check. After uploading, confirm each clip is really in OpusClip and not corrupted. Then confirm every clip is scheduled on the correct day of the coming week at the correct time, with sales at 12 PM and 8 PM and rejections at 9 AM, 2 PM and 5 PM. Confirm the caption is attached to each one. Then message me that the week is scheduled.



All times are Michigan/Detroit Eastern Time, not your local time. Before you schedule anything, check that the time zone setting in OpusClip is on Eastern. If you are in Asia you are roughly 12 hours ahead of me, so if that setting is wrong, a 9 AM post goes out at 9 PM my time and the entire week is wrong.



One more thing on delivery. In your first weeks, done means the file is in the folder and it plays. Once you are publishing, done means it is uploaded, it plays, and it is scheduled. Not exported. Not sitting on your desktop. Not "finished." I have had dead files delivered and found out the morning they were supposed to go live. If it is in the folder I am going to assume it is good.



Before the ongoing work starts there is a paid test. I pay $25 flat for 5 clips, and I pay you whether or not I hire you. That $25 is a one-time test payment, not the ongoing rate. If you make my shortlist I will also send you my full training videos covering my editing workflow and settings, and I will ask you to send me a summary in your own words before the test.



Before you apply, please do all 5 of these things, because I will ignore any application that skips a step.



First, open my Instagram, which 
 and watch 3 videos.



Second, write one sentence telling me what specific product I am selling and who I am selling it to. Name the product.



Third, write the word CUSTARD at the top of your application.



Fourth, send me a short screen recording, under 60 seconds, using Loom or any screen recorder. Open one clip that you edited yourself, play part of it, and talk over it explaining why you cut where you cut and what you removed. Your voice is enough, you do not need to show your face. Do not introduce yourself, do not tell me about your experience, and do not send me a portfolio. Just one clip and your reasoning. There is no attachment button on this site, so upload it to Loom, Google Drive or Dropbox and paste the link directly into your message.



Fifth, answer these four questions. How many minutes does it take you to edit one 60 second video from raw footage? How many hours per day do you actually have available, and what else is using your time right now, including school, other clients, and family? What is your time zone and what hours of the day do you work? Can you commit to at least 4 weeks?



Please do not send a copy paste application, because I read all of them.



You also need good written and spoken English. We will be messaging most days about which clips work and which do not, so I need to be able to explain things and know that you understood. I am not looking for perfect English, but I need you to be comfortable having a real conversation.



After I read the applications I will shortlist 3 people, send them my training videos, and run the paid test. All 3 get the same raw footage and make 5 clips from it. Whoever's editing matches my style the best gets the ongoing work. This is steady work every single week and I want one editor to stay with me for a long time.

title: Business Loan Sales Consultant / Closer — Warm Leads — AU Day Shift
description:
JOB OVERVIEW



Have you sold business loans, mortgages, asset finance or insurance? Bring your closing experience to Ezy Pzy Finance and help Australian business owners access funding.

We also welcome proven sales professionals from other industries who can demonstrate consistent target achievement and experience closing business over the phone.

You’ll receive warm enquiries, product training, weekly coaching and the opportunity to earn commission on both new and repeat clients.





YOUR EARNING OPPORTUNITY



•During probation: AUD $500/week + commissions + bonuses (approx. ₱97,500/month fixed base). After 8 weeks probation: AUD $650/week including PhilCare allowance + commissions (approx. ₱126,750/month fixed pay).

• Our agents currently average AUD $5,200/month (₱234,000/month) in total earnings including commissions and monthly bonuses.

• Earn between AUD $100 - $800 (approximately ₱4,500–₱36,000) commission per deal..

• Repeat business stays with you: when a client you funded returns for more funding, you handle their next deal and earn commission again.

• Earn additional monthly performance bonuses based on KPI’s achieved.

After your two-month probation, benefits include the base salary increase, an HMO allowance, paid annual and sick leave, and access to higher bonus tiers.





WHO WE ARE



Ezy Pzy Finance is a fast growing Australian business finance company connecting business owners with a panel of non-bank lenders.

We’re growing our remote sales team and looking for consultants who combine strong closing skills with clear communication and disciplined follow-up.

Learn more: 





WHAT YOU’LL DO



• Call Australian business owners who have already expressed interest in funding.

• Understand their business, funding needs and timing.

• Qualify enquiries and guide clients through the application process.

• Explain available options clearly, handle objections and move deals towards settlement.

• Keep your pipeline organised and follow up consistently.

• Build relationships that generate repeat business.



Warm leads are provided. There is no cold prospecting or list building, but the role involves regular outbound calls and persistent follow-up.





WHO SHOULD APPLY



You have at least two years of phone-based sales experience and have personally been responsible for closing sales and achieving targets.



We particularly welcome sales experience in:



• Business lending or merchant cash advance campaigns.

• Australian or US mortgage and asset finance.

• Insurance, debt solutions or other financial products.



Successful closers from other industries are also encouraged to apply. Show us what you sold, your targets, your results and your role in winning the business.



You should be able to:



• Build trust and communicate confidently in spoken English.

• Run a discovery conversation and ask useful follow-up questions.

• Explain products clearly and handle objections professionally.

• Own your pipeline, maintain accurate records and follow through.

• Learn new products and apply coaching.



Finance processing, customer service or appointment-setting experience is useful, but you must also demonstrate personal closing experience.





TRAINING AND SUPPORT



Your first four weeks include structured product and sales training, with an initial focus on smaller loan facilities up to approximately A$30,000.

You’ll progress to larger deals as you meet quality and settlement milestones, supported by weekly one-to-one sales coaching.





SCHEDULE AND SETUP



• Monday–Friday, 6:30am–4:30pm Philippine time.

• One-hour lunch break; 45 working hours/week.

• Fully remote, with evenings free.

• Reliable computer, internet connection and backup internet/power arrangements required.





HOW TO APPLY



Incomplete applications will not be considered. Complete applications get a response within 48 hours.

Provide ALL 5 of the following:

A short video (3–5 minutes, Loom / Google Drive / unlisted YouTube link) in two parts:



Part 1 — introduce yourself, your sales experience, and the results/KPIs you achieved (numbers, not adjectives).



Part 2 — a 2-minute mock opening of a discovery call: pretend you’ve just dialled an Australian business owner from Ezy Pzy Finance — do your opening, build rapport, and start qualifying them for funding.



- Link to your resume.

- Screenshots of your DISC assessment and IQ test results (tests available at 
/testcontent).

- Screenshot of your internet speed test, provider, and PC/laptop specs.

- Your backup internet and power solutions.

- Shortlisted candidates will be invited to a Zoom interview, including a live discovery-call role-play.





If you’re a top performing sales professional and have the self drive to earn big commissions and grow in a company that is focused on long term success, then submit your application and we’ll see if we’re a good fit to work together.

title: AI-Native Software Architect — Senior Full-Stack IC
description:
Location: Remote — Philippines

Schedule: Part-time initially, with a path to full-time

Working hours: Full overlap with Los Angeles/Pacific Time working hours

Starting compensation: $7–$12 USD per hour, based on experience

Reports directly to: Founder and CEO



Executive Summary



Bellaura is seeking an experienced AI-Native Software Architect who can personally architect and ship production features at exceptional speed using tools such as Codex and Claude. This is a hands-on senior individual-contributor role for someone who can translate business requirements into technical architecture, direct AI development workflows, and ensure the resulting software is secure, maintainable, tested, and production-ready. The role can expand substantially in scope, compensation, and ownership as the company grows and becomes funded.



The Opportunity



Bellaura is an early-stage technology platform for creators, creative professionals, events, collaboration, and bookings. You will work directly with a technical founder and a team that includes experienced Microsoft engineers.



Much of the application has been developed through AI-assisted engineering. We are now looking for someone with deep software-engineering experience who can dramatically increase our development velocity without sacrificing quality.



This is not a traditional architect role focused on diagrams, meetings, or managing other engineers. You will make architectural decisions and personally implement major features using AI as an engineering multiplier.



What You Will Do

Translate business and product requirements into clear technical requirements.

Architect and implement major features across the frontend, backend, and database.

Use Codex, Claude, and related tools to accelerate development significantly.

Break large initiatives into coherent, AI-executable implementation plans.

Provide AI agents with the context, constraints, patterns, and acceptance criteria needed to produce reliable code.

Run multiple agents or parallel development workflows where appropriate.

Review and correct all AI-generated code before it reaches production.

Design secure PostgreSQL schemas, authorization rules, APIs, and application flows.

Build with security, privacy, performance, feature gating, testing, observability, and safe rollout in mind.

Lead major refactors while preventing inconsistent patterns and unnecessary technical debt.

Maintain architecture documentation that helps both engineers and AI agents understand the codebase.

Diagnose difficult production issues and improve engineering standards as the platform grows.

Current Technical Direction



The current platform is directionally built around:



React and TypeScript

Vite

Supabase

PostgreSQL

Authentication, storage, and realtime functionality

Automated testing

CI/CD and production deployment workflows



Direct experience with every current technology is not required. However, you must be able to understand an existing codebase quickly, identify architectural risks, and begin shipping high-quality work without requiring extensive supervision.



Required Qualifications

At least eight years of professional software-engineering experience.

Bachelor’s degree in computer science, software engineering, or a closely related field.

Advanced React and TypeScript experience.

Strong PostgreSQL and relational data-modeling expertise.

Experience designing production systems at meaningful scale.

Strong system-design and software-architecture judgment.

Experience providing technical leadership, setting standards, or guiding architectural decisions.

Excellent written and spoken English.

Ability to personally implement substantial production features—not only design or delegate them.

Availability to work entirely within Los Angeles/Pacific Time business hours, which will generally require overnight working hours in the Philippines.

Strong understanding of security, authorization, privacy, testing, performance, and production reliability.

AI-Native Engineering Requirements



We are not looking for someone who occasionally asks ChatGPT to generate a function.



You should be able to demonstrate experience with several of the following:



Using Codex, Claude Code, or comparable agentic development tools on real production systems.

Dividing complex features into effective prompts, tasks, and validation stages.

Supplying agents with architecture documents, coding standards, schemas, and repository context.

Managing large refactors through AI without losing consistency or introducing hidden regressions.

Detecting hallucinated APIs, insecure implementations, incorrect assumptions, and poor architectural decisions.

Coordinating multiple agents or parallel workstreams safely.

Using tests, type checking, code review, and manual validation to verify generated work.

Structuring repositories and documentation so future AI-assisted development becomes faster and more reliable.



The best candidate will view AI as a powerful execution layer while understanding that experienced engineering judgment remains essential.



Strongly Preferred Background



We strongly prefer candidates who have also worked as a:



Business Analyst

Product Manager

Technical Product Manager

Product Owner

Founder or technical co-founder

Senior engineer with substantial product ownership



Formal titles are not mandatory. What matters is your ability to take an incomplete business objective, identify missing requirements, understand the user experience, make sound tradeoffs, and convert it into a technical plan that can be implemented successfully.



Experience with Supabase, row-level security, marketplaces, social platforms, booking systems, payments, automated testing, CI/CD, or feature-flag systems is also valuable.



The Type of Engineer Who Will Succeed



You will likely succeed in this role if you:



Ship quickly without treating security or quality as optional.

Can move from an ambiguous idea to a production-ready implementation.

Make practical architectural decisions rather than overengineering.

Challenge unclear or risky requirements while still maintaining momentum.

Investigate problems independently before escalating them.

Understand where AI can accelerate development and where human review is indispensable.

Communicate tradeoffs clearly to a business-oriented founder.

Take ownership of outcomes rather than only completing assigned tickets.

Prefer building and shipping over spending excessive time in meetings.

Growth and Compensation



The position will begin part-time and can move toward full-time based on performance, product needs, and company growth.



Bellaura is currently unfunded, so the initial compensation is $7–$12 USD per hour. We want to be direct that this is below the long-term compensation expected for someone operating at this level.



For a proven performer, our current intention is to increase compensation significantly after funding, with a target of approximately $20 USD per hour, subject to funding, performance, expanded responsibilities, and a formal compensation agreement. Equity may also become available later for someone who demonstrates exceptional long-term value.



This opportunity is best suited to someone who values early ownership, direct influence over the product, and the ability to establish themselves as a critical technical leader before the company’s next stage of growth.



Selection Process



Qualified candidates may be invited to:



Interview directly with the founder.

Review and discuss a realistic system-design problem.

Demonstrate an AI-assisted development workflow.

Review flawed AI-generated code and identify risks.

Complete a short paid technical exercise.

Provide professional references.

How to Apply



Please submit your resume, LinkedIn profile, GitHub or portfolio links, hourly-rate expectation, availability, and answers to the following three questions. Keep each answer concise and specific.



1. Describe the most substantial production feature or refactor you have completed using Codex, Claude, or another AI development system.



What were you building, how did you structure the work for AI, what context did you provide, and how did you verify the resulting code? Explain what you personally architected, reviewed, corrected, and shipped. Include links, diagrams, screenshots, or a short demonstration when available.



2. How would you architect a feature-gated event-ticketing system with promoter attribution?



Assume users can purchase tickets, promoters receive trackable links, hosts can approve attendees, rejected attendees may require refunds, and access must be protected by user roles.



Briefly describe:



The core PostgreSQL entities and relationships.

Authorization and privacy controls.

How you would prevent duplicate purchases or attribution errors.

The three most important failure cases.

Your testing and rollout strategy.



We are evaluating your reasoning, prioritization, and ability to translate business behavior into a reliable technical design—not the length of your answer.



3. Describe a time you converted an ambiguous business requirement into a successful production system.



What was initially unclear? What questions did you ask? Which technical and product tradeoffs did you make? What did you personally implement, and what measurable result did the finished system produce?

title: GoHighLevel + AI Automation Systems Assistant
description:

Systara LLC is an AI implementation and operations consultancy. We help small and mid-sized businesses organize their CRM systems, automate workflows, manage lead pipelines, and build practical reporting systems. Our clients include service businesses across several industries.



The Role

Deep, hands-on GoHighLevel experience is the first priority. You should also have practical experience connecting business processes to AI and automation tools. The right person will be organized enough to manage follow-ups, documentation, open issues, and routine operational work without needing constant supervision.



Responsibilities



You will build and troubleshoot GoHighLevel workflows, pipelines, funnels, forms, calendars, custom fields, custom values, tags, and
 or SMS follow-up systems. You will maintain client subaccounts, test automations before launch, diagnose failures, and keep system documentation current.



You will also help develop AI-assisted workflows using tools such as OpenAI, Claude, n8n, Make, Zapier, APIs, and webhooks. These workflows may classify leads, summarize requests, route information, draft internal outputs, update CRM records, or alert a team member when human review is required.
